source_text:
δεστέρων, ἀναθρώσκουσιν εἰς τελειότητα, τὴν ὡς ἐν Χριστῷ νοουμένην. Τέλειοι γὰρ εἰς ἡλικίαν οἱ κριοὶ, τῆς νοητῆς τελειότητος τὸ μέτρον, ὡς ἔν γε σφίσιν αὐτοῖς εὖ μάλα κατασημαίνοντες. Δύο δὲ οἱ κριοὶ, διττὴ γάρ πως ἐν ἡμῖν ἡ ἐν Χριστῷ τελειότης, ἡ ὡς ἐν ἔργῳ τε καὶ γνώσει νοουμένη. «Ὃς γὰρ ἂν ποιήσῃ καὶ διδάξῃ,» φησὶν, «οὗτος μέγας κληθήσεται ἐν τῇ βασιλείᾳ τῶν οὐρανῶν.» Οἶνος δὲ τοῖς ἱερείοις ἐπιχεῖται πάλιν· ἕψεται γὰρ πάντως τοῖς εἰς τελειότητα τὴν ἐν Χριστῷ νοουμένην διᾴττειν ἐσπουδακόσι, τὸ κατευφραίνεσθαι δεῖν. «Οἶνος γὰρ,» φησὶν, «εὐφραίνει καρδίαν ἀνθρώπου.» Καὶ χίμαρος μὲν ὑπὲρ ἁμαρτίας ἐσφάζετο· προσεπάγονται δὲ καὶ ἀμνοὶ δύο μετὰ τῶν ἄρτων, εἰς θυσίαν σωτηρίου. Καὶ τί τὸ χρῆμα πάλιν; Ἀπέθανε γὰρ ὑπὲρ τῶν ἁμαρτιῶν ἡμῶν ὁ Ἐμμανουὴλ, ὡς ἐν τῷ χιμάρῳ γραφόμενος, ἱερὰν δὲ ἡμῶν καὶ εὐπρόσδεκτον ἀποτελῶν τήν τε εἰς καινότητα ζωὴν καὶ τὴν εἰς νέον φύραμα μεταβολὴν, καὶ τὴν μέχρι ψυχῆς καὶ σώματος ἀνάθεσίν τε καὶ καθιέρωσιν, ἣν ὑπομένειν εἰθίσμεθα, μονονουχὶ καὶ συναποθνήσκοντες τῷ δι' ἡμᾶς ἐν νεκροῖς, ἵνα συζήσωμεν αὐτῷ. Τοιοῦτόν τι καὶ ὁ Παῦλος ἡμῖν ὁ σοφὸς ἐπιστέλλει λέγων· «Ἢ ἀγνοεῖτε, ὅτι ὅσοι ἐβαπτίσθημεν εἰς Χριστὸν Ἰησοῦν, εἰς τὸν θάνατον αὐτοῦ ἐβαπτίσθημεν; Συνετάφημεν οὖν αὐτῷ διὰ τοῦ βαπτίσματος εἰς τὸν θάνατον αὐτοῦ· ἵνα ὥσπερ ἠγέρθη Χριστὸς διὰ τῆς δόξης τοῦ Πατρὸς, οὕτω καὶ ἡμεῖς ἐν καινότητι ζωῆς περιπατήσωμεν.» Οὐκοῦν ἐσφάγη μὲν ὑπὲρ τῶν ἁμαρτιῶν ἡμῶν αὐτὸς, συντεθάμμεθα δὲ καὶ ἡμεῖς αὐτῷ, θάνατον ὑπομένοντες, οὐ σωματικὸν, ἀλλὰ νεκροῦντες τὰ μέλη τὰ ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς, καὶ κόσμῳ μὲν ζῶντες οὐκέτι, Χριστῷ δὲ μᾶλλον, καὶ δι' αὐτοῦ τῷ Πατρί. Ὅρα τοίνυν σφαζομένῳ τῷ χιμάρῳ συναποθνήσκοντας τοὺς ἀμνοὺς, καὶ συνθυμιωμένους τοὺς ἄρτους· δεκτὴ γὰρ ἡμῶν ἡ καθιέρωσις, καὶ εἰς ὀσμὴν εὐωδίας ἡ νέα τε καὶ εὐαγγελικὴ ζωὴ, συμπλαττομένη τρόπον τινὰ τοῖς παθήμασι τοῦ Χριστοῦ, καὶ τὴν αὐτοῦ μίμησιν ὑποτρέχουσα. «Εἰ γὰρ συμπάσχομεν, καὶ συμβασιλεύσομεν· εἰ συναποθνήσκομεν, καὶ συζησόμεθα· καὶ εἰ κοινωνοὶ παθημάτων ἐσμὲν, μερισταὶ καὶ τῆς εὐκλείας ἐσόμεθα καὶ αὐτοί.» Σωτηρίου δὲ θυσία διακεκλήσθω, φησὶν, ἡ τοιάδε καλῶς. Σώζει γὰρ τοὺς ὑπὲρ ὦν τὴν σφαγὴν ὑπέμεινεν ὁ Χριστὸς, εἴπερ ἐξίστησιν ἁμαρτίας, καὶ θανάτου, καὶ φθορᾶς ἀμείνους ἀποτελεῖ τοὺς συντεθαμμένους αὐτῷ καὶ συναποθνήσκοντας, κατά γε τὸν ἤδη προειρημένον τρόπον.
{ΠΑΛΛ.} Ὡς βαθὺς ὁ λόγος, καὶ ἀμυδρὸν τοῦ νόμου τὸ χρῆμα!
{ΚΥΡ.} Αἴνιγμα γὰρ, ὦ Παλλάδιε, καὶ οἱονεὶ λεπτῶν τε καὶ διεσμιλευμένων ἐννοιῶν, ἀσυμφανὲς ἀποσκίασμα.
{ΠΑΛΛ.} Εὖ ἔφης.
{ΚΥΡ.} Τρεῖς μὲν οὖν καιροὺς ὁ νόμος ἔφη, καθ' οὓς ἂν ἡμᾶς ἑορτάζειν πρέποι. Τρεῖς γὰρ, φησὶ,
pass_a_gloss: (being wont to master manfully the) more earthly things, they leap up into perfection, the one understood as in Christ. For complete in age the rams, marking very well as in themselves the measure of the spiritual perfection. And two the rams, for double somehow in us the perfection in Christ, the one understood as in work and knowledge. 'For whoever does and teaches', he says, 'this one will be called great in the kingdom of the heavens.' And wine is poured upon the victims again; for it will surely follow for those eager to dart into the perfection understood in Christ, the need to be gladdened. 'For wine', he says, 'gladdens the heart of man.' And a he-goat was slaughtered on behalf of sin; and two lambs are also brought with the loaves for a sacrifice of salvation. And what the matter again? For Emmanuel died on behalf of our sins, as drawn in the he-goat, and making sacred and well-acceptable our life into newness and the change into new dough, and the dedication and consecration as far as soul and body, which we are accustomed to undergo, all but also dying together with the one among the dead because of us, so that we may live together with him. Such a thing also the wise Paul writes to us saying: 'Or do you not know that as many as were baptized into Christ Jesus were baptized into his death? We were buried with him then through the baptism into his death; so that as Christ was raised through the glory of the Father, so we too may walk in newness of life.' Therefore he himself was slaughtered on behalf of our sins, and we too have been buried with him, undergoing death, not bodily, but deadening the members on the earth, and living no longer to the world, but rather to Christ, and through him to the Father. See then the lambs dying together with the he-goat being slaughtered, and the loaves burned together; for acceptable our consecration, and for a smell of sweet savor the new and evangelical life, molded together in a way with the sufferings of Christ, and running under the imitation of him. 'For if we suffer together, we will also reign together; if we die together, we will also live together; and if we are sharers of sufferings, we too will be partakers also of the glory.' And let such a one be well called, he says, a sacrifice of salvation. For it saves those on behalf of whom Christ endured the slaughter, since he removes from sin, and makes better than death and corruption those buried together with him and dying together, according to the manner already said before. pass_b_english: Cyril: …more earthly, leap up to the perfection understood as in Christ. For the rams, full-grown in age, mark very well in themselves the measure of spiritual perfection. And the rams are two, for perfection in Christ is in a way twofold in us, understood as in deed and in knowledge. ‘For whoever does and teaches,’ it says, ‘he shall be called great in the kingdom of heaven’ (Matthew 5:19). And wine is poured over the victims again; for gladness must surely follow those who are eager to speed toward the perfection understood as in Christ. ‘For wine,’ it says, ‘gladdens the heart of man’ (Psalm 104:15).

And a male goat was slaughtered for sin, and two lambs are brought besides with the loaves as a sacrifice of salvation. What is the meaning of this in turn? Emmanuel died for our sins, depicted in the goat; and he makes holy and acceptable our new life of newness, our change into new dough, and the offering and consecration, reaching to soul and body, which we are accustomed to undergo, all but dying together with the one who for our sake was among the dead, so that we may live with him. Paul the wise writes something of this kind to us, saying: ‘Or do you not know that all of us who were baptized into Christ Jesus were baptized into his death? We were buried with him, then, through baptism into his death, so that just as Christ was raised through the glory of the Father, so we too may walk in newness of life’ (Romans 6:3–4). So he himself was slain for our sins, and we too were buried with him, undergoing a death that is not bodily, but putting to death the members that are on the earth (Colossians 3:5), no longer living to the world, but rather to Christ, and through him to the Father.

See, then, the lambs dying together with the goat as it is slain, and the loaves burned together with them; for our consecration is acceptable, and the new life of the gospel is a fragrant odor, molded in some way together with the sufferings of Christ and running on in imitation of him. ‘For if we suffer with him, we shall also reign with him; if we die with him, we shall also live with him’ (2 Timothy 2:11–12); ‘and if we are sharers in the sufferings, we too shall have a part in the glory.’ Such an offering, it says, is rightly called a sacrifice of salvation. For Christ saves those for whom he endured the slaughter, since he takes them out of sin and makes those buried with him and dying with him superior to death and corruption, in the way already described.

Cyril: It is a riddle, Palladius, and, as it were, a dim shadow-sketch of fine and finely carved ideas.

choices.english: a sacrifice of salvation. For Christ saves
choices.why: The pun on σωτήριον / σώζει is the point of the sentence.

choices.term: «Εἰ γὰρ συμπάσχομεν ... τῆς εὐκλείας ἐσόμεθα καὶ αὐτοί.»
choices.english: cited 2 Timothy 2:11–12 for the first two clauses only
choices.why: Cyril's quotation blends 2 Timothy 2:11–12 with a third clause close to Romans 8:17 and 2 Corinthians 1:7; no single verse confirms it.
νοητός as opposed to the bodily ripeness of the rams.
